stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 5 inactives: Moore ruled out for Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists.

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 5 Buzz

Week 5 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 5

Biggest concerns on Monday Night
DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore is out for Monday Night Football against the Rams. It is his first time missing a game due to injury since 2020. That leaves Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Skyler Bell and called up from the practice squad, Trent Sherfield as the Bills receivers with Joshua Palmer also out this week. I would prefer to play Coleman of the bunch as he brings more upside. Coleman has been the Bills most productive receiver when Moore's missed time. That includes last week when he went for 116 yards and a touchdown. However, Shakir, who was the Bills top target in 2025 before Moore arrived, is a safer floor play. Those in deep leagues who rolled the dice on Moore may have no choice but to take a shot on Bell. This also means more volume for Dalton Kincaid, who likely will be the top target for Josh Allen tonight.

From earlier in Week 5
Players in London
Dallas Goedert, TE, Eagles (knee): Goedert was able to return to practice this week, albeit in a limited fashion. Still, he is active for Week 5. He should operate as the top target for Jalen Hurts, especially in the red zone. Some names to play Goedert over this week are Brenton Strange, Dalton Schultz and Michael Mayer.

Players with early starts
ACTIVE

Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Bengals (concussion): Chase was able to practice this week, so it's no surprise to see him active for Sunday. Obviously, since Chase is playing, you're starting him. Tee Higgins (adductor) was a DNP to start the week but returned to action in full on Friday. He is also active and should be started by fantasy managers.

Ashton Jeanty, RB, Raiders (ankle/foot): The Raiders' star RB popped up on the injury report Thursday after logging a limited session. He did not practice on Friday but is active for Week 5. Since Jeanty is playing for the Raiders, he should start for your fantasy football team.

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots (knee): Stevenson was able to log limited practice sessions this week and is active for Week 5. Expect the Patriots' backfield to remain a split. Stevenson is the "safer floor" option, with TreVeyon Henderson being the "home run-hitting" play against a Raiders defense that has allowed explosive runs to RBs at the sixth-highest rate.

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints (back): Kamara is active for Week 5. He should once again operate as the Saints' lead back. While he needs catches and touchdowns to make up for his inefficiency, volume has him in play as an RB3/flex option.

Cam Skattebo, RB, Giants (shoulder): Skattebo was limited at practice, wearing a red noncontact jersey to start the week. Still, he is active for Sunday's game. Skattebo is one of the safest bets for volume each week and should be started as an RB2, even in a tough matchup on paper. Plus, with bad weather potentially in the forecast, he could even see an uptick in usage.

Isaiah Likely, TE, Giants (knee/groin): Likely was limited to start the week but is indeed active for Week 5. Likely has seen a 33% target share with Jameis Winston under center. That duo is coming off their best game together. Plus, the Commanders have allowed the most passing touchdowns in the league. It's a good setup for Likely, who is the Giants' top red zone option. He should be started with confidence.

Malik Nabers, WR, Giants (knee): Nabers sat out Wednesday's practice because of soreness in his knee but is active for Week 5. This seems like something fantasy managers need to get used to, as midweek rest days could become a frequent sight this season. Nabers is coming off his best game of the season and should comfortably be started this week.

Carnell Tate, WR, Titans (back): Tate was added to the injury report Thursday, which caused a scare in the fantasy community. However, he is active for Week 5 and should be started. He has seen his target rate continuously climb, reaching 43% in Week 4. Not only that, but 26 out of his 32 targets have come against zone coverage, which the Texans have played on 83% of their plays. Lastly, the Texans are top two in both yards and touchdowns allowed to receivers.

Jayden Daniels, QB, Commanders (elbow): Daniels has been practicing with a brace on his left elbow and is active for in Week 5. Though there is some added risk here, fantasy managers should look to get Daniels back into their starting lineups. Even if the Commanders have fewer designed runs for their star QB, the upside is too high to get away from. Daniels is a top-five QB option in Week 5.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, Commanders (groin): JCM joined seemingly all of his teammates on the injury report this week. He had been limited this week but is active for Week 5. The Giants have allowed 99 RB rushing yards per game and allow explosive runs at the third-highest rate (12.5%). With Daniels coming off his injury and bad weather in the mix, do not be surprised if the Commanders run more than usual. Plus, game script could be on his side. Croskey-Merritt is a high-upside flex option.

Rachaad White, RB, Commanders (shoulder): After missing Week 4, White has been able to return to the practice field. He is active for Sunday. That likely puts some restraints on JCM's fantasy value. Still, Croskey-Merritt is the preferred option of the two Commanders backs. Consider both to be flex options in a favorable matchup.

Terry McLaurin WR, Commanders (hamstring): McLaurin is active but will not be a "full go" (as reported by ESPN's Mike Garafolo). Given the fact that hamstrings run a risk of flaring up, paired with the fact that the Commanders are playing in wet and slippery conditions, it's tough to trust McLaurin. I would advise trying to get away from him if you have the capability. I'm certainly sitting him for teammate Croskey-Merritt.

With Stefon Diggs not playing, the Commanders could be thin at receiver this week. Antonio Williams (eight targets last week) would be a sleeper flex option, likely operating as the top Commanders target. Chig Okonkwo, who was limited at practice this week but will play, would be a sleeper tight end for those in need of a streaming option.

INACTIVE

Jordan Addison, WR, Vikings (hamstring): Addison returned to practice this week after sitting out Wednesday. However, he is inactive today. Star wideout Justin Jefferson (ankle) was also listed as questionable earlier in the week but is, as expected, active. Addison's absence could provide a boost in volume to Jauan Jennings, although he has struggled to establish himself in Minnesota. If you take a shot on any other Viking, let it be T.J. Hockenson.

Rico Dowdle, RB, Steelers (toe): Dowdle is inactive for Week 5. Jaylen Warren has thrived with Dowdle sidelined, and I would expect him to continue to do so. Warren can be started with confidence once again this week.

Players with late starts
Ladd McConkey, WR, Chargers (foot): Despite missing practice this week, McConkey is active for Week 5. Denver will be without their top two corners, which helps the upside case for McConkey. Still, given how banged up he has been, he comes with more risk than usual. Given that risk, along with how lackluster the Chargers' passing attack has been, I would still look to avoid McConkey -- and would rather go with someone like Arizona's Kendrick Bourne.

Players on Sunday night
Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (foot): Flowers is active for Week 5. Those of you who waited this out should start him. In 10 career games with Tyler Huntley he has averaged six targets, 4.6 catches and 66 yards per game. He scored four touchdowns in those games.

Ruled out before Sunday
Marvin Harrison Jr., WR, TBD (set to be traded): Harrison will be inactive for Sunday's game as the Cardinals have announced they are in the process of finalizing a trade for their underperforming receiver.

Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens (ankle): The two-time MVP had his ankle rolled up last week and is in jeopardy of missing a couple of games. It's unfortunate because Jackson has been playing at a very high level. He's working a career high in yards per attempt (10.1) and completion percentage (70.8%) while averaging 58 rushing yards per game. With him out, Huntley will start for the Ravens, but he's more suited for superflex leagues. Some streaming options this week for managers in need are Jacoby Brissett, Jameis Winston and Aaron Rodgers.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (thumb/toe): Monangai will be out for Week 5. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler has reported that Monangai is dealing with "turf toe" and could possibly even miss another week or two. D'Andre Swift continues to deal with a knee injury. Although he has not missed any time due to his injury, his fumbling woes have caused his coach some concerns. Swift should see even more volume and is a must-start fantasy RB1 with Monangai out.

Pat Surtain II, CB, Broncos (ankle): Neither Surtain nor Riley Moss has practiced this week and both are out for Week 5. That would certainly make life easier for all Chargers pass catchers, if you're into that sort of thing.

Rashawn Slater, OT, Chargers (ankle): The Chargers tackle is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks because of a high ankle sprain. This just makes it tougher to trust Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton. I would look to avoid both of those players against a tough Broncos defense. Additionally, OT Joe Alt suffered a neck injury and has not practiced this week. It's very tough to trust any Chargers this week.

Quentin Johnston, WR, Chargers (chest): The Chargers receiver is out for Week 5 against the Broncos. That should lead to a bump for Harris and the other available Chargers pass catchers. Still, given their offensive woes and O-line injuries, the Chargers should be avoided by fantasy managers this week.

Mack Hollins, WR, Patriots (calf): Hollins has not practiced this week and has been ruled out for Week 5. That makes Romeo Doubs, who had nine targets last week, even more appealing. Doubs should be started over Deebo Samuel Sr., Roman Wilson, KC Concepcion and Courtland Sutton.

Saquon Barkley, RB, Eagles (hamstring): Barkley exited last week's game and is out for Week 5 because of a hamstring injury. The Eagles also placed RB Tank Bigsby on IR this week, leaving Will Shipley as their lead back. Fantasy managers may need to use Shipley this week but should look to avoid him if possible. He faces the Jaguars, a team that has allowed the fewest RB rushing yards per game -- and just one rushing touchdown all season.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): Smith is out for the Eagles' London matchup against the Jaguars. That leaves Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon as the team's top receivers. Still, no Eagles pass catcher reached as many as 35 yards last week and the team will now be operating without two expected starters on the offensive line. While one could opt to simply pivot to Dallas Goedert, it's probably best to seek options elsewhere to replace Smith.

Michael Pittman Jr, WR, Steelers (foot): Pittman has aggravated a foot injury and has been placed on IR. He had been off to a slow start, so fantasy managers should have already been looking in another direction. This means more run for Roman Wilson, who has become a Rodgers favorite of late. Wilson is a deep-league flex option in a favorable matchup.

Stefon Diggs, WR, Commanders (hamstring): Diggs, who saw nine targets last week, did not practice this week because of a hamstring injury that will keep him out for Week 5. With Terry McLaurin also up in the air, the Commanders are suddenly looking very thin at receiver. Antonio Williams (who saw eight targets last week) would be a sleeper flex option, likely operating as the top Commanders target. Chig Okonkwo, who was limited at practice this week but appears likely to play, would be a sleeper tight end for those in need of a streaming option.

stories.headline: Lampard: Coventry 'feet on the ground' after Newcastle win
stories.summary: Coventry City boss Frank Lampard is not allowing his side to get carried away after they earned a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle United on Monday.
stories.body:
Coventry City boss Frank Lampard is not allowing his side to get carried away after they earned a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle United on Monday.

Jack Rudoni tucked away a sixth-minute penalty after Lukás Hornícek brought down Sidiki Cherif inside the area which gave the hosts a halftime lead.

The Sky Blues made a quick start to the second period as well, and Cherif doubled their lead before Sven Botman's belter halved the deficit with 20 minutes to go -- making for a nervous atmosphere

But Coventry were able to wrap up their first home Premier League win in 25 years courtesy of further efforts from Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni, and make it back-to-back wins for Lampard's newly promoted men.

Lampard, whose side moved up to 14th in the table with the win, was over the moon with his side's performance, but wants them to stay grounded with another "tough" challenge against Tottenham on the horizon.

He said: "We are going to be a relative underdog in pretty much every game, so we have to maximise everything beyond the limit. It's a good feeling for the players.

"They need to keep their feet on the ground because the next one is tough and the one after that is tough. We looked like a team that was hard for teams to come here (and beat) tonight. That's the feeling we haven't had in our first home games this season.

"This gives good confidence, so it's a balance of confidence against over-confidence for us.

"They have to stay humble to that and understand. Every part of the level has gone up."

Coventry failed to score in their first four league matches, but it seems Lampard's side have now broken the shackles after netting five times in their last couple of outings.

Four different players got on the scoresheet, a pleasing sign for Lampard who saw his team finish highest scorers in the Championship last season.

He added: "It's not a nice feeling, looking at the table and seeing zero goals before Forest.

"Your left-back who hardly scores [Jay Dasilva], scores at Forest, it's a lovely story but we need more. It's great and I think it'll be great for lads going forward to feel that confidence.

"Good for all the players that scored and good for the team to feel that we can rely on that."

Another 4-1 defeat for Newcastle means they have now conceded the joint most goals in the league so far alongside Bournemouth and Chelsea.

Boss Matthias Jaissle made it clear that the result was not acceptable, but feels they were better than when they lost by the same scoreline to Leeds a month ago.

He said: "I think it was a tough story throughout the whole match. There were elements in both boxes where we need to step up and improve.

"It's not something we can compare with the Leeds match today because I think we were at least better.

"The goals we conceded, it was a different story. We were better after the first 10 minutes, we dominated the game but conceded easy goals, which we need to improve.

"If you conceded eight goals in two away matches on Monday evenings, then it's not good enough for the Premier League."

The loss leaves Newcastle 11th in the Premier League, with eight points from their first six matches.

Information from PA was used in this report.

stories.headline: Noah Ostlund scores go-ahead goal in third period in Sabres' 5-3 win over Panthers
stories.summary: — Noah Ostlund scored the go-ahead goal on the power play 7:15 into the third period, and the Buffalo Sabres defeated the Florida Panthers 5-3 on Monday in an outing both teams lost key players to injury.
stories.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. -- — Noah Ostlund scored the go-ahead goal on the power play 7:15 into the third period, and the Buffalo Sabres defeated the Florida Panthers 5-3 on Monday in an outing both teams lost key players to injury.


Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin scored his second goal of the season before not returning after sustaining an upper-body injury early in the second period.


Coach Lindy Ruff listed Dahlin as day to day, while adding the defenseman won't initially join the team in opening a three-game road trip at Montreal on Tuesday.


Meantime, Panthers starting goalie Jacob Markstrom did not return after allowing two goals on 11 shots in the first period. He was replaced by Akira Schmid, who finished allowing three goals on 21 shots.


Coach Paul Maurice said Markstrom felt something tighten, and downplayed the severity by saying: “There's no injury there.”


Buffalo also got goals from Tage Thompson, Josh Doan and Ryan McLeod in an outing the Sabres never trailed.


Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen allowed one goal on 14 shots for the win in a backup role. He entered 6:25 into the second period after starter Colten Ellis allowed two goals on nine shots. Ellis was pulled after Sam Reinhart tied the game at 2 by poking in a loose puck that dribbled into the crease behind the goalie.


Reinhart scored twice and Anton Lundell also had a goal. Brady Tkachuk got his first point with the Panthers as he assisted on Reinhart's second goal.


Florida (2-2-2) has dropped two straight following a 4-1 home-opening loss to Minnesota on Saturday.


With the game tied at 3, Ostlund scored by tapping in Zach Benson’s pass through the crease. Buffalo converted two of five power-play opportunities after opening the season going 1 of 17.


The Panthers converted two of four power-play chances after entering the game 1 of 28.


Up next
Panthers: Travel to play Columbus on Tuesday night.


Sabres: Follow a five-game homestand to play at Montreal on Tuesday night. ------

stories.headline: Carrick backs Man United for UCL rebound amid challenging spell
stories.summary: Michael Carrick said Manchester United will turn things around ahead of their Champions League game at Atlético Madrid on Tuesday.
stories.body:
Michael Carrick said Manchester United are in the middle of a "challenging, stickier" spell but he "totally believes" players will turn things around ahead of their Champions League game at Atlético Madrid on Tuesday.

United have only won two out of eight matches in all competitions so far this season, with back-to-back draws with Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur following defeats to Manchester City and Brighton in the last month.

The Champions League is an opportunity for Carrick to change that dynamic, having beaten Sabah 4-0 on matchday one, and now visiting Atlético at the Metropolitano.

"Of course we hoped for a lot more [this season], we expected a lot more, but we are where we are," Carrick said in a news conference on Monday. "I was aware there was going to be a period when it was going to become a bit more challenging, a bit stickier. That's part of it. Football and building something takes a journey. You've got to overcome things.

"I understand that when it's not going too well, there's a real clamour and a real feeling of 'it's a disaster, it's all wrong and everything needs to be changed.' I kind of get that, but that's not our mindset, certainly not mine.

"I love this part sometimes, when it's going against you, you see who's really there, within the group, the squad, the club, who wants to be here for the long term. The supporters are desperate for it and we've got to give them something. You've got to embrace challenges to get where you want to be. I totally believe we'll come through it."

Carrick inspired a turnaround in United's 2025-26 season when he took over as head coach from Ruben Amorim in January, and the team's performance in the second half of the campaign persuaded United to give him the position full-time.

However the side's Premier League form, with one win in six games leaving them 13th in the table, already has the former United midfielder feeling the heat.

"It depends how you define pressure," he said on Monday. "We know what we want and what we're capable of doing as a team.

"We want to be part of something successful, there's no negativity about that. There's going to be times when it's a bit of a struggle, but to get anywhere, to do something good, something great, you've got to be able to do something difficult, and get through it."

United drew 1-1 with underperforming Tottenham at Old Trafford on Saturday, conceding a 92nd-minute equaliser, despite Spurs playing the latter stages of the game with 10 men.

"It's very fine lines," Carrick said. "The last three goals we've conceded in the league have all been avoidable. It's very fine margins. But I've got the utmost confidence in the boys that we can win games, and win a lot of games."

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: The Valkyries' wild path from expansion team to the Finals
stories.summary: Two years ago, the Valkyries didn't exist. Now they're competing for their first title -- here's how they did it.
stories.body:
As a general rule, expansion teams aren't really supposed to be very good right away. Sure, the initial player draft offers a chance to assess the league's potentially undervalued and overlooked players on the off chance of finding a hidden treasure, but from there, contention usually requires a lot of patience: A bunch of losing seasons provide the high draft picks to slowly accumulate talent, with a legitimate chance to contend finally waiting at the end of that long building process.

The Golden State Valkyries apparently missed that memo.

Barely two seasons into their existence, the Valkyries are headed to the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream (Game 1 at 12:30 p.m. Saturday). To get there, they closed out the Las Vegas Aces on the road. This was a matchup that began as a huge mismatch in team pedigree -- the Aces had won three of the past four WNBA titles, while Golden State literally didn't exist two years ago -- if not talent. Instead, it became a changing of the guard, with the league's new contender sweeping aside one of its greatest dynasties.

Exactly how historic are the Valkyries as a recent expansion team? And how have they managed to go from an expansion draft to a Finals appearance in less than two years? Let's dive into five charts that explain Golden State's unprecedented rise.

Going into 2025, it was a bit of a mystery how the Valkyries would end up doing in their first WNBA season. Previously, expansion teams had posted an average winning percentage of .306 with a minus-8.4 net rating (we're not including 1997, the league's first season). If history was any indication, fans could expect Golden State to be one of the league's worst teams out of the gates.

But before Golden State, the league hadn't added a new team since the Atlanta Dream in 2008, meaning a backlog of great players was building up in competition for the same number of total roster spots in the W. (Witness the number of high draft picks who would be waived heading into each season.) Contrary to the historical record, this suggested the Valkyries would be tapping into a vast reservoir of available talent when building the first WNBA expansion squad in nearly two decades.

And that has largely proved to be true. The Valkyries ended up having the second-best first-year winning percentage (.523) of any WNBA club -- trailing only the 1998 Detroit Shock (.567) -- and the best expansion year by both net rating (plus-1.8) and Elo rating (1494). And all they've done since is continued that meteoric rise, to the point that they had the best regular season for a second-year team by all available measures of team quality, and in fact finished with the second-best record in the league -- and best net rating overall -- in 2026.

As a result of their dramatic rise from, well, not having a team at all in 2024 to the league's top net rating in 2026, the Valkyries' odds of winning the WNBA title also have risen dramatically. Going into the season, Golden State looked like a solid pick to return to the playoffs and possibly even win a series (last year's season ended with a 2-0 first-round sweep to the Minnesota Lynx). But contending for the championship seemed like a much taller order -- especially in a crowded field that contained the former champion Aces and Liberty, plus the improved Olivia Miles version of the Lynx, an Indiana Fever team featuring a healthy Caitlin Clark, and the overhauled Dream.

And for the first few months of the season, that seemed about right. The Valkyries were 13-7 through the end of June, one of the better records in the league but still clearly within a five-team logjam below Minnesota and Las Vegas. It seemed as if Golden State were destined to spend all year fighting for razor-thin seeding margins within that group. But since July 1, the Valkyries rattled off a league-best 19-5 record and saw their odds in statistical systems like Elo zoom past those of the presumed-favorite Lynx by the end of the regular season, when the latter hit a late slump. A 5-1 playoff start has only reinforced their status as a serious title threat, and now the early-season underdog Valkyries are statistical favorites to win it all.

If we had to pick a single calling card for the Valkyries' impressive championship bid, it has to be their defense. With a defensive rating of 100.6, they not only led all teams in suppressing opponents' per-possession scoring, but the gap between Golden State and No. 2 Atlanta at 104.5 (3.9 points per 100 possessions) was roughly the same as the gap between Atlanta and No. 7 New York at 108.7 -- or nearly the gap to league average itself, which was 109.1. The Valkyries' difference compared to that league figure (minus-8.5 points per 100) ranked as the sixth-best single-season WNBA defense ever relative to average.

The 2025 Valkyries landed on a number of top-tier defenders through the expansion draft, including Veronica Burton on the perimeter and Temi Fagbenle on the inside, helping Golden State rank fourth on defense right out of the gate under coach Natalie Nakase. But an even more refined version of the team's D came into shape in 2026, with names like Kiah Stokes -- whose block saved the Valkyries in Game 2 against Vegas -- and Gabby Williams joining Burton this season.

The Valkyries' defensive recipe blends a few components. They have one of the better rim protectors in the league in Stokes, which contributes to a league-low 47.8 effective FG% allowed, plus a couple of premier ball hawks in Burton and Williams, which forces opponents into mistakes -- they also ranked No. 2 in turnover rate forced. And opponents don't get many easy transition opportunities against Golden State because the Valkyries play at the league's slowest pace and hardly ever turn the ball over. Nakase was the lead assistant under Becky Hammon for the 2023 Aces when they had one of the best defenses in WNBA history -- and now she's using those lessons to try to dethrone her old team.

Obviously, a team doesn't post the league's best net rating and fight to within a game of the WNBA Finals without star performances, and the Valkyries absolutely got one of those this season from Burton.

The Northwestern alum was originally taken No. 7 by Dallas in the 2022 draft, but the Wings never really gave her much opportunity to earn an expanded role; she started 19 only total games in her first two seasons, averaging a paltry 14.5 minutes over that span before being waived before the 2024 season. After signing with Connecticut midseason, Burton continued to log backup minutes (12.7 MPG) despite improving her scoring efficiency with increased usage.

It wasn't until Burton, left unprotected in the expansion draft, landed with Golden State that she finally found a situation in which she could start -- and she has thrived in the role. Averaging 29.0 MPG as a Valkyrie, Burton has remained one of the league's top defensive guards while also taking a huge step forward as an offensive presence, which earned her Most Improved Player honors in 2025. But the advanced metrics in particular adore Burton for her two-way play; her ability to draw fouls while still taking plenty of 3s; her playmaking (she maintained a 34.5% assist rate with just an 11.9% turnover rate); and her massive on-court impact, which showed up at both ends of the court. Burton finished the season ranked second behind only the MVP A'ja Wilson in both LAKER wins added and win shares.

Burton had help. Led by Williams, who arrived from Seattle as a big-time impact player in her own right, six additional Valkyries beyond Burton had at least 2.5 LAKER wins added; no other team in the league had more than five players crack that barrier, much less if their top star is tossed out. Add in Nakase, the 2025 WNBA Coach of the Year, and the Valkyries are loaded with talent from top to bottom.

As much as we've been extolling the virtues of Burton's game, she hasn't been as effective as usual in the playoffs -- averaging just 9.5 PPG on 35.3% shooting from the field in six games. She has still made her trademark on-court impact; Golden State has a plus-12.4 net rating when she's in the game, 13.3 points per 100 better than when she sits. And in the clutch, she made multiple big shots when Golden State needed her. But her postseason LAKER rating of plus-2.7 points per 100 is markedly down from her mark of plus-7.5 in the regular season.

Luckily for the Valkyries, they've received big performances from some of the other names on the roster -- most notably Williams, who is averaging 22.7 PPG in the playoffs. Another player who has run with an opportunity in Golden State, Williams was always more of a defensive player than a scorer in her previous career stops, but her usage rate this season (29.0%) was a whopping 11.2 points higher than her previous career average, and she's pushing it even higher (to 32.1%) in the playoffs.

Of course, Williams does have a tendency to raise her game in the postseason (where her career scoring average of 14.5 PPG is markedly higher than her 9.3 regular-season figure), but this is taking things to a new level. And the other Valkyries to raise their output significantly in the playoffs are Tiffany Hayes and Cecilia Zandalasini, who both have produced massive LAKER ratings (Hayes is at plus-10.7!) in around 18 minutes per game off the bench.

It should be noted that the Valkyries' run has involved its fair share of gritty wins, surviving Dallas in a win-or-go-home Game 3 to win in the first round, needing some late free throws and a last-second block to take the 2-0 lead over Las Vegas, and then outlasting the Aces in overtime of the semifinals clincher. There's no question Golden State will have another tough assignment taking down Angel Reese and the Dream -- and the league's second-best defense -- to win a title.

But the Valkyries have spent their entire, brief existence defying conventional expectations for expansion teams. Why should the most significant step yet along their improbable path to a championship be any different?

stories.headline: Toto Wolff finds quirky solution to Kimi Antonelli track limits 'stress'
stories.summary: Toto Wolff joked he would shove a pillow under the a--e of Kimi Antonelli before hailing the Italian's maturity as he moved within reach of the world championship.
stories.body:
Toto Wolff joked he would shove a pillow under the a--e of Kimi Antonelli before hailing the Italian's maturity as he moved within reach of the world championship.

Antonelli claimed third place under the lights in Singapore on Sunday to stretch his advantage in the drivers' standings to 102 points ahead of Mercedes teammate George Russell.

That opens the possibility that the 20-year-old could confirm his place as Formula 1's youngest world champion at the next round in Texas in a fortnight. As things stand, he would need to win at the Circuit of the Americas with Russell ninth or lower and Lewis Hamilton fifth or lower.

Antonelli's dominance of the season has been remarkable, especially given his difficult debut campaign last year, and he is all-but certain to clinch his place in the sport's history books over the next few races.

He has, though, proved that he has a penchant for pushing track limits. He again received a final warning for the violation in Singapore, as he has done on several occasions this season, with one more fault leading to a penalty.

Mercedes boss Wolff has a solution as he admitted it causes tension on the pit wall.

"I have a good strategy, I'm going to put a pillow from the hotel under his a--e, under his butt, so he can actually see the road," Wolff said.

"Because I think it's like this, you know, he can't see it [the track].

"So yeah, under his a--e so he can see, and it stresses us. Half the race we already have three strikes, but it also shows that he's pushing the limits a lot."

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Red Bull downplay 'team to beat' label by George Russell, Oscar Piastri

- Lando Norris takes responsibility for collision with Oscar Piastri in Singapore: 'I let McLaren down'

Antonelli was off the pace for much of the weekend in Singapore but profited from the McLaren pair colliding to take fourth in Saturday's sprint before making late moves to rise from fifth to third in Sunday's main event.

Max Verstappen completed a perfect weekend, backing up sprint victory with a dominant race. The four-time world champion remains 119 points adrift, with Antonelli admitting it would be "very scary" if the Dutchman were in the title fight.

Antonelli was on the radio during the race to ask about issues he felt with the car but battled on to ultimately stand on the podium. Russell recovered to ninth after having to start from the back of the grid.

"I think how he [Antonelli] has driven is mature and good," Wolff added. "We talked about it and he said, 'I've just got to keep my calm here and make sure that I finish the race.'

"So handling a difficult car at that stage and trying to develop it and learn, it's good."

It remains a possibility that the penultimate round in Qatar could be cancelled and the season finale in Abu Dhabi replaced by Imola -- if F1 bosses decide they cannot race in the Middle East due to the ongoing conflict.

If that happened, 25 available points would be off the table, moving the Italian ever closer to the championship.

"I haven't looked at it from that perspective because at the moment I have the thought of how many points is it actually and when could he win it?" Wolff said.

"The aim must be to score points, not to lose too many on the others.

"And then it's going to come towards him. And whether that's in Mexico or Brazil or further down the line, we shall see.

"And I guess whether Qatar and Abu Dhabi happens at the moment, everybody says so. You need to go the direction of this is six more races to go and not four."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Monday Oct. 12
Suns land Schubert, Butler from Hawks

The Suns have landed their offseason trade target in Aidan Schubert from Hawthorn, in a package also involving Sam Butler and some picks going both ways.

Gold Coast gained Schubert, Butler, Hawthorn's 2028 first-round pick, and Hawthorn's 2027 third-round pick, in exchange for Gold Coast's 2028 first-rounder, and second rounders in both 2027 and 2028.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley says he's not mulling QB change entering bye
stories.summary: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley is not considering a quarterback change heading into their Week 6 bye, but he did say the passing offense must improve.
stories.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley is not considering a quarterback change heading into their Week 6 bye, but he did say his team's passing offense must improve.

Speaking to reporters Monday, Hafley reiterated that Malik Willis will remain the team's starting quarterback, and he is not considering a change to backup Kyle McCord. However, particularly after Sunday's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, during which the Dolphins struggled to move the ball through the air, Hafley acknowledged the team must be able to pass the ball more effectively.

"Malik needs to be better, OK? And that's not the headline," Hafley said. "The headline is we all need to be better, and I mean that. I thought yesterday for the first time we ran the ball really well and we moved the ball. We ran for 200 yards against a really good team. But everything in the pass game has to be better, right? It's the receivers, it's the tight ends, it's the protection. It all has to tie in, and it all has to be better.

"And that's the quarterback, that's the coaches, that's the offensive line, that's the running backs, that's the tight ends. This is a team game that we all need to be more efficient, and we need to be better. And we will work through that. I have confidence in the coaches, I have confidence in the players that we have. We will work through that and we will get better. It's been five weeks."

Willis ranks 31st in the NFL with a 56.2% completion percentage and 23rd in quarterback rating (43.9). Through five games, he has thrown for 849 yards and two touchdowns against four interceptions.

The onetime third-round pick has also rushed for 186 yards and two touchdowns, albeit with five fumbles.

Willis has lost fumbles in each of his past three games, which is an area Hafley said the team will focus on during the bye week.

"We got to look hard at it during the bye week," Hafley said. "We talk about ball security all the time and we work on it and we've got to do a better job of putting him in those situations and he's got to have the awareness to protect the ball as well. We'll take a hard look at fixing that because we're not going to win games if we're fumbling the ball like that."

The Dolphins' offense is the youngest in the NFL, with three rookies receiving consistent playing time. Their offensive line, which returned its top four starters from a season ago, ranks middle of the pack in terms of protection with a 50.8% pass block win rate. But Willis is the fifth-most contacted quarterback in the league, and the fourth-most sacked.

He got off to a slow start in Sunday's loss, at one point throwing more interceptions than completions before ultimately finishing with 137 yards and a touchdown on 15-of-27 passing.

Miami enters its bye week on a five-game losing streak to start the season and Willis said the week needs to focus on self-reflection and accountability if the team is to earn its first win since Dec. 28.

"I think we just got to watch the tape and figure it out. And that's the thing that I think Coach Haf does great," Willis said. "He holds everybody accountable and he's honest with us. If we need to do better, we need to do better. And if we got to execute, we need to execute. We got to figure out a way to get guys on the same page because there's just a lot left out on the field that could be better than what it is."

stories.headline: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope cites team chemistry as key to 76ers' success
stories.summary: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope says the 76ers' success this season depends on how well the team's diverse personalities mesh.
stories.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- On a team loaded with star power and championship expectations, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope said the Philadelphia 76ers' success this season depends on how well their diverse personalities mesh.

"Our chemistry is gonna be the biggest part for us," Caldwell-Pope said Monday. "Us liking each other, being able to be around each other and have fun on and off the court."

After agreeing to a buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies in July, Caldwell-Pope signed a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Sixers.

Caldwell-Pope, 33, has perhaps the best perspective on meshing personalities on a new team aiming for championship contention, especially one with LeBron James. He has won two championships in his career, one with the James-led Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 and another with the Denver Nuggets in 2023.

The veteran said that the bonding process has already begun in earnest with dinners that will ramp up as the season goes on.

"We have so much talent from one through 12, or 15, however many guys we've got, and it's talent everywhere," he said. "So, I think our biggest thing is just communicating with each other, learning each other's tendencies, and just trying to implement that on and off the court."

Caldwell-Pope is entering his 14th season in the NBA. Over his near decade-and-a-half in the league, he has established himself as one of its best 3-and-D players. He'll look to continue that role in Philadelphia as the Sixers contend for a title, but he is coming off one of the worst seasons of his career.

Caldwell-Pope underwent surgery to address a misalignment of his right pinkie finger in February and missed the last 31 games of the season. Before the injury, he averaged 8.4 points, 2.7 assists and 2.5 rebounds over 21.3 minutes in 51 games for the Grizzlies, his fewest minutes and points per game since his rookie year. His 31.6% from 3-point range last year was the second lowest of his career.

stories.headline: St. Louis unbeaten run up to 20 games, tying Red Bulls' MLS record
stories.summary: Carlo Holse's hat trick helped St. Louis City SC beat the LA Galaxy 6-2 on Sunday night to extend their unbeaten streak across all competitions to 20 games.
stories.body:
ST. LOUIS -- Carlo Holse's hat trick in the first 21 minutes -- the second hat trick in club history -- helped St. Louis City beat the LA Galaxy 6-2 on Sunday night to extend their unbeaten streak across all competitions to 20 games and tie the MLS record.

St. Louis, which is 13-0-5 in its last 18 regular-season games, tied the mark set when the New York Red Bulls went unbeaten in an MLS-record 20 consecutive games across all competitions in 2016.

Rafael Navarro converted from the penalty spot in the 45th minute, scored again in the 53rd and added two assists for St. Louis (14-6-8). Lukas MacNaughton scored on a diving header in the seventh minute of first-half stoppage time and Roman Bürki had five saves.

Holse opened the scoring in the second minute, added a goal in the seventh and skipped a shot inside the right post from the center of the area to make it 3-0 in the 21st minute to record the second-fastest hat trick in MLS history. Hany Mukhtar scored three goals for Nashville in the first 16 minutes of 5-1 win over Chicago on July 17, 2021.

The Galaxy's Kyōgo Furuhashi went off due to an apparent hamstring injury and was replaced in the 10th minute by João Klauss, whose goal in the 71st minute capped the scoring. Klauss, a 29-year-old midfielder in his first season with the Galaxy, had St. Louis City's first hat trick in a 3-3 tie with the Galaxy on June 14, 2025.

Robert Taylor scored in the 31st minute for the Galaxy (9-11-9).

St. Louis beat the Galaxy 3-1 on July 22 at Dignity Health Sports Park and hosts the Vancouver Whitecaps on Wednesday in a Western Conference top-of-table clash.

The Galaxy, who are clinging to the last playoff spot in the West, play the Portland Timbers at Dignity Health Sports Park on Wednesday. The Timbers are three points behind the Galaxy for ninth place -- the final playoff spot.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Location of Dream home games for WNBA Finals still uncertain
stories.summary: The Dream, dealing with conflicting events at State Farm Arena, are still determining where they will play their home games during the upcoming WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
The location of the Atlanta Dream's home games for the WNBA Finals had not been determined as of Sunday night.

The Dream, who will face the Golden State Valkyries in the best-of-seven series, are scheduled to host Games 3, 4 and 6 (if necessary) on Oct. 22, 24 and 29. The Dream's home arena since 2021 has been Gateway Center Arena at College Park, which holds only 3,500 fans. That small capacity is a concern for the Finals, but at this point, the Dream have not said if they have secured a larger facility.

Dream president and chief operating officer Morgan Shaw Parker, speaking to the media last week, said the team was "finalizing details on their home venue and where we will be playing" for the Finals. The Dream and the WNBA did not offer further details Sunday when contacted by ESPN.

The Valkyries will host Games 1, 2, and also 5 and 7 (if necessary) at their home, the Chase Center in San Francisco, which has a capacity of 18,064.

This year, the Dream moved six regular-season home games and all three of their previous home playoff games to State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta -- which will also be the team's full-time home next season. The capacity there is 17,044. But State Farm is booked with a Sombr concert on Oct. 22 and Atlanta Hawks regular-season games on Oct. 24 and 29.

The Dream previously were based at State Farm (then known as Philips Arena) from the franchise's inception in 2008 to 2016. Refurbishments at the arena led to the Dream playing at Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion in 2017-2018. The arena's name was changed to State Farm in 2019, and the Dream returned there for that season. Then the Dream relocated to the much smaller Gateway Center in 2021.

But the WNBA's and the Dream's increased popularity have prompted the move back to State Farm starting in 2027. The Washington Mystics played three games of the 2019 WNBA Finals at their home, CareFirst Arena, which seats 4,200. That was the last time the WNBA Finals were played at a venue that had fewer than 8,000 seats except 2020, when the entire WNBA season was played in a COVID-19 bubble facility without fans in Bradenton, Florida.

Several playoff games in the past, including in the WNBA Finals, have been played in alternate venues during the league's 30-season history because of facility conflicts or renovations. The Dream hosted a 2013 WNBA Finals game at the Arena at Gwinnett Center in Duluth, Georgia. That facility is now known as Gas South Arena and seats around 13,000.

There also have been WNBA Finals games played at college arenas such as Eastern Michigan (2008), University of Illinois Chicago (2014), USC (2016), Minnesota (2017) and George Mason (2018).

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: Ranking every AFL free agent by the impact they'll have at their new club
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL free agency period is now complete. We've ranked every move that has been made, factoring in positional needs and their likely impact for season 2027.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL free agency period is now complete, with seven players finding new clubs either as restricted or unrestricted free agents.

We've ranked every move that has been made, factoring in positional needs and their likely impact for season 2027 (not the rest of their career). So, who will be the biggest needle mover of the bunch in the immediate future?

7. Kieren Briggs
This is absolutely no criticism of Kieren Briggs, but there really aren't many players in the competition (if any) that could be dropped into the Tigers in 2027 and be serious needle movers. Remember, Richmond has won just 10 games across the last three seasons and is widely expected to finish in the bottom four once again next year. Tigers skipper Toby Nankervis will remain the club's primary ruck in the immediate future, but the arrival of Briggs will allow for a new-look one-two punch. The former Giant is one of the best hitout-to-advantage rucks in the game and an elite clearance winner. At 27 years of age, and with Nankervis now 32, Briggs' impact will likely be felt in the years beyond 2027.

6. Jordon Butts
Key defensive stocks have been a concern for the Bulldogs in recent years, so the signing of Jordon Butts will be a welcomed addition for the club. Butts makes the move after eight seasons and 94 games with the Crows, but he's managed just 10 and nine games in 2025 and 2026. Throughout different parts of the last couple of years, he's struggled with unlucky injuries; in 2025 it was a collapsed lung, and this year he battled concussion and a fractured foot. With the continued strong form of Josh Worrell and Mark Keane, and emergence of Josh Borlase at the Crows, a move to the Bulldogs makes sense for both the 26-year-old Butts and the Dogs.

5. Joel Amartey
The Blues landed key forward support for Harry McKay in the form of Joel Amartey, who crosses from the Swans as an unrestricted free agent. It's a shrewd acquisition for Carlton, and the club will be hopeful he can be an upgrade on both Brodie Kemp and Mitch McGovern. Amartey is coming off a season at Sydney in which he booted 28 goals from 15 games and averaged three marks per game. In 2024 he enjoyed a career-best 43-goal campaign, including a bag of nine against the Crows. Amartey is just 27 years of age and should only really be coming into his prime as a key position player in the AFL. Could surprise a few in 2027.

4. Toby Greene
Another year, another major coup for the Cats. Is anyone surprised?! Former Giants captain Toby Greene joins Geelong as an unrestricted free agent while GWS has to make do with second-round compensation. We all know Greene has been a high-impact player throughout his 15-year career and he will add a whole new dynamic to the Cats' forward line, one that features former Giants teammate and close friend Jeremy Cameron. In 2026, Greene kicked 34 goals -- his lowest return in a season since his injury-interrupted 2020 campaign -- but did amass over 20 disposals per game. If anyone wanted to argue he deserves the top spot on this list I wouldn't scoff, but it's not as if the Cats had trouble scoring in 2026...

3. Ben King
It may have been a move that surprised few, but it's one -- along with the signing of Zach Merrett, of course -- that will have Hawks fans believing a premiership is possible in 2027. For a fair chunk of the 2026 season, King looked to be the Coleman Medal winner. Gold Coast's capitulation didn't help his chances, though he still finished the home and away season with 60 goals to his name -- the third consecutive year he's managed 55+ goals. King will partner veteran Jack Gunston and dynamo Nick Watson in what now looks to be one of the most dangerous forward lines in the game.

2. Lachie Neale
The Lachie Neale-Brisbane Lions era is over, with the two-time Brownlow Medal winner joining Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent and partnering reigning Brownlow winner Nick Daicos in a new-look Magpies midfield. Neale might be 33 years of age and on the downturn of his decorated career, but he still averaged 29 disposals, 12.5 contested possessions, and six clearances per outing in 2026 and figures to be a major contributor next season in a Collingwood engine room that's often lacked depth and firepower. Even if the Magpies receive 80-85% of this season's production from Neale, he'll be difficult to top as the most impactful free agent of the year.

1. Zak Butters
The most sought after man in football made the decision to sign with the Bulldogs during free agency. Former Power star Zak Butters joins the club as a top five player in the game, and at age 26, you can certainly make the argument he's only at the beginning of his prime. Butters will partner Western Bulldogs skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in what's easily the most impressive and dynamic three-pronged midfield in the competition. He offers a real point of difference, too, with his electric pace and the ability to break lines two eye-catching features that have seen him ascend to footy superstardom.
